FARRA:v3p272/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p272/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p272/r6.claim: The most God-fearing person is Abū Bakr.

TUSTARI:92:17-18/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r1.claim: The most Godfearing is the truthful one, identified as Abu Bakr: others gave and feared, but he let go of the perishable and kept the everlasting.

TUSTARI:92:17-18/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:92:17-18/r2.claim: When the Prophet asked what he had kept for himself, Abu Bakr answered: God and His Messenger.

TAB-FULL:v24p478/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r2.claim: The most Godfearing person will be kept from the blazing Fire; al-atqā is used with the sense of al-taqī.

TAB-FULL:v24p478/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r3.speaker: طرفة بن العبد
TAB-FULL:v24p478/r3.claim: Tarafa's use of awḥad for “alone/one” supports the substitution of an afʿal form for a faʿīl form.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#2/r1.speaker: عروة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3441#2/r1.claim: Urwa says the verse concerns Abu Bakr, who freed seven enslaved people tortured for God, including Bilal and others.

SULAMI:v2p399#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p399#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p399#2/r1.claim: The pious are ascetics, and the most pious abandon the world entirely; Abu Bakr gave away the transient world and kept God and His Messenger, as he said in response to what he left for himself.

THALABI:v10p218#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218#2/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v10p218#2/r5.claim: They take al-atqā as the opposite of al-ashqā, and cite poetry showing that a negated predicate can mean 'not alone'.

THALABI:v10p219/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r1.speaker: عروة عن أبيه
THALABI:v10p219/r1.claim: Abu Bakr freed Bilal and other persecuted people; the passage is said to concern him, and he spent all of his forty thousand in charity.

THALABI:v10p219/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
THALABI:v10p219/r2.claim: He says Abu Bakr bought and freed vulnerable slaves; when his father advised buying someone to protect him, Abu Bakr said he was pursuing his own aim, and the verse was revealed about him.

THALABI:v10p219/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p219/r3.claim: He recounts Bilal's monotheistic defiance while being tortured, the Prophet's reassurance, and Abu Bakr's purchase of Bilal with gold.

THALABI:v10p219/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p219/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v10p219/r4.claim: He recounts that Abu Bakr obtained Bilal by trading him for Nustas, a wealthy enslaved man who refused Islam; God then declared Abu Bakr's emancipation was solely for His sake, to be repaid in the hereafter.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r4.speaker: ابن الزبير
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p455/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reports that Abū Bakr’s father asked him to buy slaves who would protect him, but Abū Bakr said protection was not his aim; the source connects this to the pious giver passage.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r1.claim: Sayujannabuha means God will remove him far from the Fire and place him apart from it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r2.speaker: جميع المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r2.claim: They identify the most pious one as Abu Bakr, who is moved far away from the Fire.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p88/r3.claim: The most pious person is sincere in affirming God's oneness.

WAHIDI-QT:92:17/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:17/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:17/r1.claim: God will keep the most God-fearing person away from Hell, identifying him as Abu Bakr.

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r7.claim: Yujannabuhā means that the pious person is moved far enough away from the Fire to be on the opposite side.

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r8.claim: Al-atqā may mean simply the pious, or the most pious among the people of Paradise, where children, the insane, the compensated, and houris are also present.

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r9.claim: The warning and promise address morally responsible people; thus children and the insane are also kept from the Fire without being included as the warned audience.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r7.claim: The most God-fearing person will be kept away from the fire; الأشقى and الأتقى mean the wicked and pious person.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r2.speaker: ابن الزبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p448/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says Abu Bakr bought and freed vulnerable slaves; when his father urged him to buy someone who could protect him, Abu Bakr replied that protection was precisely what he sought.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r1.speaker: أهل التأويل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r1.claim: Exegetes identify al-atqa through the end of the surah as Abu Bakr, while the description also includes everyone who shares these qualities.

TABRISI:92:14-21/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:14-21/r6.speaker: طرفة
TABRISI:92:14-21/r6.claim: The superlative forms al-atqā and al-ashqā may simply mean a pious person and a sinful person, as a line by Ṭarafa uses awḥad for wāḥid.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152/r1.speaker: جميع المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152/r1.claim: The person kept away from Hell is Abū Bakr, according to all the interpreters.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r1.claim: The verb yujannabu means that the most God-fearing person will be kept far from the Fire.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:17-18/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the most God-fearing person as Abu Bakr, who will be kept from entering Hell.

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r5.claim: The most God-fearing is kept from entering the Fire, not merely spared its full torment; avoiding shirk alone does not guarantee this, though it does not imply enduring the Fire.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#2/r1.claim: The most God-fearing person whom God will keep far from Hell is the believer.

QASHANI:92:13-17/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:13-17/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:13-17/r5.claim: The absolutely God-fearing rejects every otherness and is absorbed in unity, escaping all levels of fire; one who stops at attributes may be forgiven yet miss the Essence’s joy and remain veiled.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the superlatives mark two great opposing figures as if Hell were made only for the worst and Paradise only for the most pious; some identify them as Abū Jahl or Umayya and Abū Bakr.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r1.claim: The most God-fearing person is pure and is moved far away from the Fire.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r5.claim: Many commentators say these verses were revealed about Abu Bakr, and some claim consensus; Ibn Kathir says Abu Bakr certainly falls within their general wording and is foremost in these virtues.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r10.speaker: الزبير بن بكار
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r10.claim: Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār reports that Abū Bakr freed vulnerable Muslims; when his father suggested buying someone to protect him, Abū Bakr said that was precisely his aim.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r11.speaker: أبو بكر
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r11.claim: The report attributes to Abū Bakr the reply that he wanted the freed people to protect him, not to purchase a worldly defender.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r12.speaker: زهرة
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r12.claim: When Quraysh blamed the idols for a freed woman’s blindness, Zahra rejected their power and her sight returned.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r13.speaker: الزبير بن بكار
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r13.claim: The report lists Abū Bakr’s freeing of al-Nahdiyya, her daughter, and a girl of Banū al-Muʾammal.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r14.claim: A report says Abū Bakr bought Bilāl from Umayya ibn Khalaf while Bilāl was tortured at midday, repeatedly crying “One, One”; the idolaters alleged a prior favor, which revelation refuted.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r4.claim: The most God-fearing has reached the peak of piety by avoiding both idolatry and sins; a lesser sinner may enter the fire and later leave.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r1.claim: The promise that Abū Bakr would be pleased connects to the promise that God’s gift will satisfy the Prophet; Abū Bakr is the closest of the community to the Prophet’s station.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r2.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r2.claim: The Prophet’s statement that God and the believers would accept only Abū Bakr supports his unique closeness and the contrast between his striving and the worst unbeliever’s.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p451/r3.claim: Some interpreters say spiritual light from night prayer and other good deeds will bring sensory light after death.

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r1.speaker: عروة
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r1.claim: He said Abu Bakr freed seven people tortured for God, including Bilal and ʿAmir ibn Fuhayra; the passage about the most God-fearing was revealed concerning him.

DURR-FULL:v8p538/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p538/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p538/r1.claim: He identified the most God-fearing person as Abu Bakr.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230/r1.speaker: عروة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p230/r1.claim: Urwa reports that Abu Bakr freed seven people who were being tortured for God, and the verse about the most Godfearing being kept away from the Fire was revealed about this.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r1.claim: The two exclusions seem in tension if ṣaly means any entry into or heat from Hell: believers who sin are neither the most wretched nor the most pious. Alusi resolves this by reading ṣaly as especially severe torment between Hell's layers.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r2.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r2.claim: Ibn al-Munir transmits lexicographers' description of ṣaly as placing an animal in a pit between layers of gathered coals, supporting the sense of especially intense torment.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the exclusion as rhetorical comparison between an eminent unbeliever and an eminent believer, not a strict exclusion of every other unbeliever or believer; al-Kashf approves, but Alusi notes its Muʿtazilite premise about sinners remaining in Hell.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r4.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r4.claim: The Judge argues that “a Fire” is indefinite, so this verse need not say that only unbelievers enter any level of Hell; Hell has different layers. Al-Zamakhshari objects that the next verse still excludes all but the most pious from that Fire.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r5.claim: A possible reply is that the Judge rejects the inferential force of descriptive restriction, so this verse does not establish a strict exclusion for him; the phrase “only the most wretched” remains harder to explain.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r6.claim: A hadith from Abu Hurayra says only the wretched enter Hell; when asked who is wretched, the Prophet describes one who neither obeys God nor leaves sin for God. Sunnis interpret such reports in light of evidence that grave sinners may be punished.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#6/r7.claim: Another proposed solution takes ashqā and atqā generically as “wretched” and “pious,” citing Tarafa's use of a comparative form to mean “one”; Alusi says this does not resolve the exclusions.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r1.speaker: طرفة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r1.claim: The continuation of Tarafa's line ends “I am not alone in that path”; Alusi says awḥad here means wāḥid, supporting use of comparatives as generic descriptors.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r2.claim: Alusi says the generic reading still fails: restricting torment to the unbeliever would imply no other person enters or is punished, against Sunni doctrine; restricting escape to the very pious would exclude sinful believers and even children, the insane, and those without property.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r3.claim: After weighing the positions, Alusi says one may prefer al-Kashf's approval of al-Zamakhshari's rhetorical reading if one does not hold that grave sinners remain forever in Hell.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p151/r4.claim: Jannaba governs two objects: al-atqā is the first and the Hell-pronoun the second, promoted to subject in the passive; the root means putting to one side and often distancing, as here.

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r8.claim: The most God-fearing avoids both disbelief and sin, is kept far from the Fire, never enters it, and passes easily onward to Paradise.

QUTB-ZILAL:92:17/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:17/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:17/r1.claim: The most God-fearing person is the fortunate counterpart of the most wretched person.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p389/r6.claim: الأشقى and الأتقى mean the most wretched and most devout in degree, a common intensifying usage.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p390/r2.claim: The relative clauses describing the most wretched and most God-fearing indicate that their deeds cause the respective verdicts; the two superlatives also form a near-rhyme.

TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r2.claim: Al-Qummi identifies the person “most pious” as Abu al-Dahdah, an interpretation the author says comes through Shia routes from the Imams.

TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r3.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r3.claim: Al-Tabarsi transmits from al-Wahidi a story in which an Ansari buys a palm tree for forty trees and gives it to the Prophet, who gives it to the home's owner.

TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r4.speaker: عطاء
TABATABAI:92:1-21#2/r4.claim: A report from ʿAta names the man Abu al-Dahdah; al-Suyuti transmits the story from Ibn ʿAbbas through Ibn Abi Hatim and calls it weak.

TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r1.speaker: الرازي
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r1.claim: Al-Razi says Sunni exegetes agree the “most pious” is Abu Bakr; he says Shia exegetes instead name ʿAli, citing 5:55, and interpret the superlative as the best human.

TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:1-21#3/r2.claim: The author rejects as an overstatement the claim that all Shia sources name ʿAli; he says the reliable Shia evidence supports Abu al-Dahdah and again rejects an absolute “best of all people” reading.

TABATABAI:92:15-20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r2.claim: The “most pious” means the person more God-fearing than others, including those wary of worldly loss or poverty: among them, the one who spends for God is most pious. The descriptor makes the interpretation general, without excluding a specific occasion of revelation.

TABATABAI:92:15-20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:15-20/r3.claim: Making “most pious” and “most wretched” absolute superlatives over all people implies that only one person, or one per age, is saved or damned, which conflicts with the general warning to everyone.

BINTSHATI:v2p115/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p115/r6.claim: Al-atqa is unrestricted here, unlike atqakum in 49:13, which is qualified by reference to the people addressed.

BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.claim: The oath's night, daylight, and creation frame divergent earthly endeavors, then contrasting afterlife fates: the denier's fire and the pious giver's satisfaction.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r5.claim: The moral opposition is now named directly through the labels al-ašqā for the damned and al-atqā for the pious.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.claim: The longer, central portrait of the pious clarifies that generosity is for ethical purification, not repayment of worldly favors, and is directed toward the Lord's face through a biblical metaphor.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:17:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:17:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:17:anmerkung/r1.claim: The phrase parallels 87:11, and atqā derives from taqwā or ittaqā as discussed for verse 5.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.claim: Verses 15–21 explain the traits of those cast into Hell and those shielded from it, together with their reward.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r3.claim: The warning addresses Quraysh: persistent deniers of truth face the blazing fire, while those who spend to attain purity are protected from it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r4.claim: The contrast is between rejecters of God’s Messengers and believers, not degrees of wickedness or piety; conclusive warning leaves Messenger-rejecters no legitimate excuse, making them the most wretched.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r1.claim: Those who heed the Messenger’s warnings, prepare for judgment, and spend to cleanse their wealth are Godfearing; the earliest companions earned the rare ranks of foremost and nearest.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r2.speaker: some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r2.claim: Some infer that only the most wretched enter Hell and less-wretched people are spared.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r3.claim: That inference fails in context; carried through consistently, it would wrongly imply that only the most pious are spared Hell or admitted to Paradise.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.claim: A pious believer need not receive a favor or gain before helping; all blessings come from God, and good should be done for God's approval alone.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r6.claim: Taqwa derives from protecting oneself against great danger; in Qur'anic usage it chiefly means avoiding evil and doing good to protect oneself from Hell.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.claim: After warning of the blazing fire in verse 14, verses 17–20 describe giving for God's sake without owing anyone, spiritual purification, and being kept from the fire.

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r3.claim: Giving charity in God's name purifies both the giver and the wealth; tazakkā shares an etymological root with zakāh.

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.claim: Others say vv. 17–21 praise Abū Bakr, who bought and freed weak slaves; when his father asked why he did not buy stronger defenders, he said he sought no defense.

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.claim: One revelation account says Bilāl was tortured after desecrating the Kaʿbah idols, kept testifying to God's oneness, and the Prophet assured him that the One would save him.

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.claim: In that account Abū Bakr bought Bilāl for gold after the Prophet told him Bilāl was tortured for God; the idolaters alleged he acted to repay a favor, prompting vv. 19–21.
